description: This research report develops Cross-Theater Conflict Coupling (CTCC) to examine how the Russia–Ukraine and U.S.–Israel–Iran wars interact through shared defense resources, technology, expertise, and policy-controlled access. Using PAC-3, Shahed–Geran, Ukrainian counter-drone assistance, Russian diesel, and strategic petroleum reserves, it distinguishes connections from verified transmission, recipient conversion, and consequential effects, including conditional war-termination scenarios.
abstract: This research report develops Cross-Theater Conflict Coupling (CTCC) as a mechanism-based framework for identifying when developments in one war produce consequential changes in another war system. Focusing on the Russia–Ukraine war and the U.S.–Israel–Iran conflict, it examines competition over shared defense-industrial resources, technology and operational-knowledge transfer, and policy-mediated changes in access and strategic choice. It specifies five conditional propositions and six claim-specific evidence gates (G1–G6), distinguishing shared interfaces, activation decisions, receipt, recipient conversion, observed decision or functional consequences, and direction-specific feedback from causal attribution. Structured comparison and process tracing examine PAC-3 MSE allocation and PURL, Shahed–Geran industrial adaptation and proposed reverse transfers, Ukrainian counter-drone assistance in Gulf states, Russian diesel authorization and shipment claims, and strategic petroleum buffers. The analysis also explores conditional scenarios of asymmetric war termination, distinguishing lower combat activity from net releasable strategic capacity after continuing obligations, production constraints, and adversarial adjustment. The report finds different levels of evidence across the cases and does not treat connections, announcements, nominal stocks, or asserted ceasefires as proof of realized cross-war gains. Its assessments are based on evidence available through October 26, 2026, and do not constitute forecasts or definitive causal estimates.

methodology.source_basis: Public official documents, institutional records, industry disclosures, contemporaneous reporting, dated legal instruments, energy and cargo signals, and structured comparative assessment of source independence and evidentiary limits.
methodology.case_context: Russia–Ukraine and U.S.–Israel–Iran conflict systems, with report-wide evidence cutoff on October 26, 2026.
methodology.core_problem: When and through what verifiable resource, technology, knowledge, or policy-mediated pathways does a change associated with one war alter usable strategic capacity, institutional decisions, or war-sustaining functions in another?
methodology.research_design: Structured focused comparison; within-case process tracing; stage-specific documentary tests; evolving no-source-war and no-policy counterfactuals; positive, negative and incomplete-pathway comparisons.

propositions.name: Effective-bottleneck transmission
propositions.claim: Cross-theater scarcity affects a target war system when a demonstrably common, non-substitutable resource bottleneck remains binding after buffers.

propositions.name: Policy-mediated anticipation
propositions.claim: Credible access-rule changes may induce independently observed decisions before physical delivery; decision consequences differ from functional capacity gains.

propositions.name: Conversion dependence
propositions.claim: Transferred equipment or expertise changes usable capability only where recipient technical, organizational and threat-specific interfaces support conversion.

propositions.name: Conditional substitution and dependency migration
propositions.claim: Rewiring and adaptation may relax one constraint while creating exposure to another component, skill or regulatory interface.

propositions.name: Adversarial and feedback qualification
propositions.claim: Durable effects depend on opponent adaptation; genuine feedback requires a dated identifiable return pathway rather than coincidence.

evidence_gates.name: Shared interface
evidence_gates.minimum: Specific supplier, stock, rule, route, productive system or expertise relevant to both theaters

evidence_gates.name: Activation
evidence_gates.minimum: Dated source-war-conditioned authorization, allocation, restriction, deployment or communicated condition

evidence_gates.name: Receipt
evidence_gates.minimum: Dated custody or material, personnel or information arrival at a defined recipient

evidence_gates.name: Conversion
evidence_gates.minimum: Identified technical, industrial, doctrinal or organizational integration

evidence_gates.name: Decision consequence
evidence_gates.minimum: Observed consequential decision or behavior of affected actor beyond the originating G2 act

evidence_gates.name: Functional consequence
evidence_gates.minimum: Observed usable capacity, output, performance or resilience change

evidence_gates.name: Feedback
evidence_gates.minimum: Dated, direction-specific return pathway with identified actors, object, control interface, and recipient-side to source-theater sequence

central_claims: Shared connection is insufficient evidence of activated cross-war transmission, recipient conversion, or causal effects.
Authorization, production, contractual allocation, shipment, receipt, operational use and attributable effect require independent records.
Cross-theater effects depend on effective bottlenecks, timing, substitution, reciprocal obligations and recipient compatibility.
Decreased hostilities or asymmetric war termination do not automatically generate net transferable strategic capacity.
The cases reveal multiple partial mechanisms and unresolved downstream evidence rather than a verified generalized mutual benefit.

dimensions.name: Shared Resource Competition and Allocation
dimensions.description: Competing inventories, suppliers, procurement authority and delivered missile variants across war systems.
dimensions.observed_pattern: Cross-theater air-defense procurement and PURL pressure are reported; object-matched Ukraine-specific MSE displacement is not identified.
dimensions.interpretation: Finite production and allocation interfaces do not alone determine realized recipient war-system effects.

dimensions.name: Adaptive Technology and Knowledge Transfer
dimensions.description: Industrial learning, variant development, personnel and military operational knowledge crossing theater boundaries.
dimensions.observed_pattern: Historical Iranian-origin Shahed production localized in Russia; reverse 2026 Geran flow unverified; Ukraine-to-Gulf personnel and software training reported.
dimensions.interpretation: Industrial or advisory transmission differs from recipient-side operational conversion and verified benefit.

dimensions.name: Policy-Controlled Access and Conditional Commitments
dimensions.description: Sanctions authorization, license scope, procurement channels, diplomatic threats, regulatory gating and energy-target restraint.
dimensions.observed_pattern: General License 135 and later legal instruments are documented while U.S. receipt, reciprocal restraint, and material benefits remain unverified at cutoff.
dimensions.interpretation: Institutional permissions and strategic expectations can change before material implementation.

dimensions.name: Energy Inventory and Strategic Buffers
dimensions.description: International petroleum reserves, U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve, national holdings, deliveries, refinery absorption and ownership accounting.
dimensions.observed_pattern: Reserve announcements and inventory observations span different stocks, dates and physical units.
dimensions.interpretation: Nominal or awarded barrels cannot be equated with freely releasable, delivered or militarily useful net capacity.

dimensions.name: Asymmetric War Termination
dimensions.description: Localized pauses, national ceasefire, prolonged fighting, territorial conquest, commitment overhang, NATO deterrence and Iran-war trajectories.
dimensions.observed_pattern: Three-by-three scenario analysis rather than empirically verified future outcomes.
dimensions.interpretation: Available strategic capacity after termination depends on residual obligations, inventories, replacement needs and evolving opposing behavior.

key_findings: Cross-war connections and institutional access do not, by themselves, establish strategically consequential cross-war effects.
PAC-3/PURL evidence supports shared industrial scarcity and reported delivery pressure, not a verified same-variant numerical diversion from Ukraine caused by the Iran war.
Historical Shahed-to-Geran industrial absorption is established; a completed 2026 model-specific Russian return shipment to Iran and its operational effects remain unverified.
Ukrainian counter-drone assistance and reported Sky Map placement/training demonstrate partial transmission; recipient-integrated performance gains and reciprocal energy flows remain unquantified.
Regulatory diesel authorization, production and tanker destination signals are not equivalent to completed U.S. customs receipt or attributable Russian military capacity gains.
International oil reserve releases, refinery use and national balance sheets have noninterchangeable accounting denominators.
Asymmetric termination does not automatically produce a peace dividend or net releasable military resources; residual obligations and opponent adaptation can offset lower consumption.
Attribution requires event-specific records, source independence, matched functional units and independently evolving counterfactuals.
policy_recommendations: Maintain owner–variant–time ledgers separating authorization, procurement, payment, production, transfer, receipt and usable inventories.
For war termination specify geographic scope, protected functions, start time, monitoring, verification, civilian access and response to violations.
Test PAC-3/PURL claims with original and revised schedules, variant/lot acceptance and recipient-level operating consequences.
Authenticate model-specific Geran manufacture-to-custody chains and recipient records before attributing 2026 reciprocal gains.
Evaluate transferred defensive software and expertise against recipient activation dates, matched threats, co-located defenses and operational performance.
Track Russian diesel by product, origin, vessel IMO, legal and customs entry, commercial receipts, fiscal effects and functional consequences.
Reconcile petroleum storage and release denominators at owner, country, physical commodity and time-window levels.
Test any nationwide termination with predeclared 1-, 4-, 12- and 26-week comparative production, consumption, stocks and delivery windows.
